statements.text: I mean, absolutely. I mean, obviously, we're just launching the caucus this weekend. But AI especially, there's a lot of bipartisan interest in this. It is going to be incredibly - not just to the popular arts, but in so many industries, be so disruptive. I mean, there's also, obviously, some opportunity. But to creative people, to this industry, there's a lot of dangers.
statements.venue: NPR interview on launching the Popular Arts Caucus at Comic-Con

statements.text: Congress has a responsibility to protect women and girls from deepfake pornography. Whether you're a pop-star like Taylor Swift or a middle schooler, deepfakes are extremely troubling, predatory, and designed to shame and intimidate. We must stop these horrific attacks. https://t.co/qk8HkOX2vJ

RFK Jr. published a health report full of errors and apparently AI-generated content. We cannot trust HHS to keep Americans safe when its leader is peddling conspiracy theories. https://t.co/MARe7asG6o

There’s going to be a lot of interest from the House Democratic Caucus to immediately begin this process,” [...] “Anytime you have folks talking about AI moving towards extinction of human life, I think that’s got to rise to the top of priorities for us in Congress.
There has to be public hearings; and we can get answers not just from those that are building this AI right now, but also the CEOs who are leading these companies.
We need to take this AI threat seriously and we need immediate action. We have an opportunity for real regulatory rules that can keep people safe. https://t.co/TmSXvGNwmn

If the American President is relying on the policy advice of a Musk-designed, Hitler-friendly chatbot with a predilection for child pornography in order to carry out his official duties, Americans have a right to know. If the United States military killed dozens of innocent schoolchildren based on the faulty advice of an AI chatbot, we have a right to know that too. And if an unelected oligarch is influencing U.S. policy through his AI-generated alter ego, Americans have a right to know how our government’s decisions are being reached.
statements.venue: Letter to President Trump from Reps. Garcia and Raskin, in Oversight Democrats press release
